issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that for each j some generator W_k has nonzero pairing with s_jj U_j. It does not show that the indices k are distinct; one W_k could have nonzero pairing with several different j. Thus r' >= r does not follow. The statement is true, but the written proof is incomplete.

issues.failure_explanation: Counterexample: take n=3, Q=I, D=diag(10,1,1), so M0=I and M1=D. Let X have transform-domain squared singular values 100, 90, 1 under M0, e.g. a 1x1x3 tube with entries 10, sqrt(90), 1. For gamma=0.95, under M0 the total energy is 191; after one component the cumulative ratio is 100/191<0.95 and after two it is 190/191>0.95, so r_gamma(M0)=2. Under M1 the energies are 10000, 90, 1; total 10091; after one component the ratio is 10000/10091>0.95, so r_gamma(M1)=1. Thus r_gamma(M0)=2>1=r_gamma(M1), contradicting the theorem. The proof incorrectly equates the M1 retained-energy ratio with the M0 error ratio.
